ARB.doc:
Arbitraries: the generator, the printer, the observer and the equality of
a type, as one record -- what QuickCheck finds by a type class and a
program here passes by name (docs/plans/quickcheck.md, D4).

members.name: arb
members.spec:
type 'a arb = {gen : 'a Gen.gen, show : 'a -> string, co : 'a -> Word64.word,
               eq : ('a * 'a -> bool) option}
members.doc:
The record of a type: `eq` is `NONE` where the type has no equality of
its own and none is given, and is then the equality of what `show`
shows.

members.name: equal
members.doc:
`equal a (x, y)` is the equality of `a`: its `eq`, or the equality of
what its `show` shows.

members.name: int
members.doc: `int` is the arbitrary of `Int.int`.

members.name: word
members.doc: `word` is the arbitrary of `Word.word`.

members.name: word64
members.doc: `word64` is the arbitrary of `Word64.word`.

members.name: char
members.doc: `char` is the arbitrary of `Char.char`.

members.name: string
members.doc: `string` is the arbitrary of `String.string`.

members.name: real
members.doc:
`real` is the arbitrary of `Real.real`, whose equality is identity.

Identity is the same number, with the zeros told apart and every NaN
equal to every other (docs/plans/quickcheck.md, D6).

members.name: bool
members.doc: `bool` is the arbitrary of `bool`.

members.name: unit
members.doc: `unit` is the arbitrary of `unit`.

members.name: order
members.doc: `order` is the arbitrary of `order`.

members.name: option
members.doc: `option a` is the arbitrary of options of `a`.

members.name: list
members.doc: `list a` is the arbitrary of lists of `a`.

members.name: vector
members.doc: `vector a` is the arbitrary of vectors of `a`.

members.name: array
members.doc:
`array a` is the arbitrary of arrays of `a`, compared by their elements:
a fresh array at every draw.

members.name: intInf
members.doc: `intInf` is the arbitrary of `IntInf.int`, drawn by `Gen.intInf`.

members.name: intRange
members.spec: val intRange : int * int -> int arb
members.doc:
`intRange (lo, hi)` is the arbitrary of the integers of `[lo, hi]`, drawn by `Gen.intRange`: a domain a law can name (D7).

**Raises** `Domain` if `hi < lo`.

members.name: wordRange
members.spec: val wordRange : word * word -> word arb
members.doc:
`wordRange (lo, hi)` is the arbitrary of the words of `[lo, hi]`, drawn as `Gen.intRange` draws integers.

**Raises** `Domain` if `hi < lo`.

members.name: reference
members.doc:
`reference a` is the arbitrary of references to `a`: a new one at every
draw, and equal only to itself, as `=` on references is.

members.name: enum
members.doc:
`enum xs` is the arbitrary of the values of `xs`, each shown as its name:
the arbitrary of a datatype with no values in its constructors. The first
is the simplest.

**Raises** `Empty` if `xs` is empty.

**Example** `#show (enum [(LESS, "LESS"), (GREATER, "GREATER")]) GREATER = "GREATER"`

members.name: vectorSlice
members.doc:
`vectorSlice a` is the arbitrary of slices of vectors of `a`: a vector,
and a start and a length within it.

Two slices are equal when their vectors have equal elements and their
starts and lengths are the same.

members.name: arraySlice
members.doc:
`arraySlice a` is the arbitrary of slices of arrays of `a`, as
`vectorSlice` draws them, over a fresh array at every draw.

members.name: array2
members.doc:
`array2 a` is the arbitrary of two-dimensional arrays of `a`.

The numbers of rows and of columns are each drawn as a length is, at the
square root of the size; an array with no rows has no columns. Two
arrays are equal when they have the same dimensions and equal elements.

members.name: exn
members.doc:
`exn` is the arbitrary of exceptions: those of the Basis Library that
carry no value, `Gen.Generated`, and `Fail` with any message.

Two exceptions are equal when they have the same name, and, for `Fail`,
the same message.

members.name: pair
members.doc: `pair (a, b)` is the arbitrary of pairs.

members.name: triple
members.spec: val triple : 'a arb * 'b arb * 'c arb -> ('a * 'b * 'c) arb
members.doc: `triple (a, b, c)` is the arbitrary of triples.

members.name: function
members.doc:
`function (a, b)` is the arbitrary of functions from `a` to `b`, of every kind of D5.

A function is pure, raises `Gen.Generated` at some arguments, or
observes its effects, which a law compares (docs/plans/quickcheck.md,
D5 C). A function has no equality and is shown as `fn`; the report
lists the calls of a counterexample's functions.

members.name: pureFunction
members.doc:
`pureFunction (a, b)` is the arbitrary of pure, total functions from `a` to `b`.

It is for a law that says its function has no effects (D5, class A).

CHECK.doc:
Running properties: many cases, each from its own seed at a size that
grows over the run, and a report.

The seed of a run is a hash of the property's name unless a seed is
given, so that a run is the same on every machine, and a failure is
reported with a token that runs its case again.

A failing case is shrunk before it is reported. The shrinker changes the
words the case read: it deletes, joins and swaps the elements of lists,
makes generated functions constants, and lowers words towards 0, the
simplest. It keeps a change only when the case still fails with the same
class and has become simpler (fewer words read, or smaller ones), so that
a `Div` never turns into an `Overflow` and the shrinking ends.

members.name: config
members.spec:
type config = {seed : Word64.word option, tests : int, maxSize : int, maxDiscards : int, maxShrinks : int,
               exhaustiveBelow : int, smallScope : int}
members.doc:
How a property is run.

`seed` is the seed of the run (`NONE`: a hash of the name), `tests` the
number of cases that must pass, `maxSize` the largest size,
`maxDiscards` the number of discarded cases after which the run gives
up, `maxShrinks` the number of runs the shrinker may make, and
`exhaustiveBelow` the most cases a property may have for every one of
them to be run instead (0: never), and `smallScope` the number of cases
of the small scope that are run before the random ones (0: none).

A property has finitely many cases when every word its case reads has
finitely many values (a `bool`, a `char`, an `Int8.int`, a choice among
a list, and tuples of these), and no length: exhaustive mode then runs
them all, at size `maxSize`, simplest first, and a failure found is the
simplest there is, with no shrinking.

Otherwise the small scope is run first: the cases in which every word
read is 0, 1 or 2 (integers 0, \~1 and 1, lengths up to 2, the first
characters, both booleans), simplest first, as many as `smallScope`
allows. A failure there is reported as exhaustive mode reports one; the
cases that pass are not counted in `tests`. A property whose values need
each other's bounds (an index one past the end of a string drawn beside
it) fails there where random cases rarely meet it.

members.name: default
members.doc:
100 cases at sizes up to 100, from a seed that is a hash of the name.

A run gives up after 1000 discarded cases and shrinks in at most 5000
runs. It runs every case of a property with at most 65536 of them
(docs/plans/quickcheck.md, P9), and otherwise first 100 cases of the
small scope (P13).

members.name: result
members.doc:
What a run found.

`Failed` has the shrunk case: `counterexample` is what it drew, as
shown, and `calls` the calls of each of its generated functions, with
`shrinks` the runs that the shrinking took. `replay` is the token of the
case as it was drawn. `Passed`'s `exhaustive` says that its cases were
every case there is.

members.name: check
members.spec: val check : config -> string -> Prop.prop -> result
members.doc: `check c name p` runs `p` as `c` says.

members.name: replay
members.spec: val replay : string -> Prop.prop -> Prop.result option
members.doc:
`replay token p` runs the case of a `Failed` result's `replay` token again, shrunk as the run shrank it.

It is the case's verdict and what it drew, or `NONE` when the token is
not one.

members.name: report
members.doc:
`report name r` is the report of a run: a first line `PASS name` or
`FAIL name`, and what the run found.

members.name: passed
members.doc:
`passed r` is `true` for a run that passed and had the coverage it asked
for.

members.name: main
members.doc:
`main ps` runs each named property with `default`, prints its report,
and ends the program with failure if one did not pass.

members.name: laws
members.doc:
`laws ls` runs the laws of a program of `runedoc --laws`, each named, and ends the program with failure if one did not pass.

Before each law it prints `LAW name`, so that a run a watchdog stops
names the law it was in, and after it the law's report. The
environment chooses how they run (docs/plans/quickcheck.md, D9 and
D13): `RUNE_PROPERTY_DEEP` runs 10000 cases for each seed from 1 to
1000, or to `RUNE_PROPERTY_SEEDS`, until one fails;
`RUNE_PROPERTY_ONLY` runs the law of that name
alone; `RUNE_PROPERTY_AT` the laws at the structure of that name;
`RUNE_PROPERTY_AFTER` runs the laws after the one of that name,
where a run that was stopped goes on; `RUNE_PROPERTY_REPLAY` runs the
case of that replay token, shrunk, and prints it. The last line counts
the laws that passed and failed.

CO.doc:
Observers: what a generated function sees of its argument (QuickCheck's
CoArbitrary, reduced to a hash). Two arguments with the same observation
get the same result from a generated function.

members.name: co
members.doc: An observer of values of type `'a`: a 64-bit word for each.

members.name: int
members.doc: `int` observes an integer: different integers are told apart.

members.name: word
members.doc: `word` observes a word.

members.name: word64
members.doc: `word64` observes a 64-bit word.

members.name: char
members.doc:
`char` observes a character.

**Example** `char #"a" <> char #"b"`

members.name: bool
members.doc: `bool` observes a boolean.

members.name: unit
members.doc: `unit` observes `()`.

members.name: order
members.doc: `order` observes an order.

members.name: string
members.doc: `string` observes a string, by a hash of its characters.

members.name: real
members.doc:
`real` observes a real by its bits: `0.0` and `~0.0` are told apart,
and so are NaNs of different bits.

members.name: option
members.doc: `option c` observes an option, and what it holds by `c`.

members.name: list
members.doc: `list c` observes a list: its length and every element by `c`.

members.name: pair
members.doc: `pair (c, d)` observes a pair by its components.

members.name: triple
members.spec: val triple : 'a co * 'b co * 'c co -> ('a * 'b * 'c) co
members.doc: `triple (c, d, e)` observes a triple by its components.

GEN.doc:
Generators: values drawn from the source of a case of a property.

A generator reads the nodes of its own part of an implicit tree of random
words, so that the parts of a value never draw from each other: that is
what lets the shrinker change one part and leave the others be
(docs/plans/quickcheck.md, D3). How a word becomes a value follows the
generator principles of that roadmap: integers are small, on an edge, or
anywhere in their range, a third each; a list's length is up to the size,
often 0 or 1. The size grows from 0 over the cases of a run.

members.name: gen
members.doc: A generator of values of type `'a`.

members.name: sample
members.doc:
`sample g seed size` is the value `g` draws from the source of `seed`
at `size`: the same value every time.

**Example** `sample (list int) 0w1 0 = []`

members.name: draw
members.doc:
`draw g (source, address)` is the value of `g` read at `address` of
`source`: what the other structures of the library run a generator
with.

members.name: return
members.doc:
`return x` always draws `x`.

**Example** `sample (return 3) 0w0 10 = 3`

members.name: map
members.doc: `map f g` draws `f x` for the `x` that `g` draws.

members.name: map2
members.doc:
`map2 f (g, h)` draws `f (x, y)` for the `x` and `y` that `g` and `h`
draw from their own parts.

members.name: bind
members.doc: `bind g f` draws `x` from `g`, and then from `f x` in a part of its own.

members.name: pair
members.doc: `pair (g, h)` draws a pair, each component from its own part.

members.name: triple
members.spec: val triple : 'a gen * 'b gen * 'c gen -> ('a * 'b * 'c) gen
members.doc: `triple (g, h, k)` draws a triple, each component from its own part.

members.name: sized
members.doc: `sized f` is the generator `f n` for the size `n` of the case.

members.name: resize
members.doc: `resize n g` is `g` at the size `n`.

members.name: oneOf
members.doc:
`oneOf gs` draws from one of `gs`, each as likely; the first is the
simplest.

**Raises** `Empty` if `gs` is empty.

members.name: frequency
members.doc:
`frequency ws` draws from one of the generators of `ws`, each as likely as
its weight says; the first is the simplest.

**Raises** `Empty` if no weight is positive.

members.name: elements
members.doc:
`elements v` draws an element of `v`, each as likely; the first is the
simplest.

**Raises** `Empty` if `v` is empty.

**Example** `sample (elements (Vector.fromList [7])) 0w5 3 = 7`

members.name: filter
members.doc:
`filter p g` draws from `g` until `p` holds, a hundred times at most,
and then gives the case up: it is discarded, as a condition that does
not hold discards it.

members.name: Discarded
members.doc:
`Discarded` is raised by a generator that gives its case up.

The runner counts the case as discarded. It is the library's own, raised
only while a case is drawn, never through the code under test.

members.name: fix
members.doc:
`fix f` is the generator `g` for which `g = f g`: a recursive generator.
`f` must make its recursive draws smaller, by `resize`, so that they
end.

members.name: intRange
members.spec: val intRange : int * int -> int gen
members.doc:
`intRange (lo, hi)` draws an integer of `[lo, hi]`.

It is a third of the time small (within the size of 0), a third on an
edge, and a third anywhere. Half the edges are the extremes (0, 1, \~1,
the bounds and their neighbours) and half the powers of two in range
and their neighbours.

**Raises** `Domain` if `hi < lo`.

**Example** `sample (intRange (5, 5)) 0w9 50 = 5`

members.name: int
members.doc:
`int` draws an integer of the whole range of `Int.int`, as `intRange`
does; where `Int.int` has no bounds, of the range of 64 bits.

members.name: largeRange
members.spec: val largeRange : LargeInt.int * LargeInt.int -> LargeInt.int gen
members.doc:
`largeRange (lo, hi)` draws an integer of `[lo, hi]` as `intRange` does, for a range of at most 2^64 integers.

The integers may be of any size: this is what the arbitraries of `Int64`
and `Position` are made of where `Int.int` is narrower.

**Raises** `Domain` if `hi < lo`, or if the range has more than 2^64
integers.

members.name: intInf
members.doc:
`intInf` draws an `IntInf.int`: a third of the time small, a third an
edge of a fixed width, a third of any magnitude.

An edge is 2^k, 2^k - 1 or 2^k + 1, or the negation of one, for `k` up
to 130. A magnitude is 1 to `size` limbs of 30 bits (the limbs of Rune's
`IntInf`), each uniform, with either sign.

members.name: intInfRange
members.spec: val intInfRange : IntInf.int * IntInf.int -> IntInf.int gen
members.doc:
`intInfRange (lo, hi)` draws an integer of `[lo, hi]`, a range of any width, as `intRange` does.

It is a third of the time small, a third on an edge (0, 1, \~1, the bounds
and their neighbours, powers of two and their neighbours), and a third
anywhere in the range.

**Raises** `Domain` if `hi < lo`.

members.name: word
members.doc:
`word` draws a word: a third of the time small, a third on an edge, a third anywhere.

Half the edges are the extremes (0, 1, the largest and its neighbour,
the top bit and its neighbours) and half the powers of two and their
neighbours.

members.name: word64
members.doc: `word64` draws a 64-bit word as `word` draws a word.

members.name: code
members.doc:
`code maxOrd` draws the code of a character of a character set of
`maxOrd + 1` characters, as `char` draws a character.

Where `maxOrd` is above 255, a third of the draws that are any of the
256 are instead any of the whole set.

members.name: char
members.doc:
`char` draws a character: half the time any of the 256.

The other half it is a letter or digit, a space or control, or a
character that the syntax of numbers, characters and strings gives a
meaning to, or the separator of paths, `/`.

members.name: real
members.doc:
`real` draws a real: a special one, a small one, or any, a third of the time each.

The special ones are the zeros, the infinities, a NaN, the smallest and
largest subnormals and normals, 1, \~1, 0.5, 2^53 and the real after it.
The small ones are integers and halves within the size. Any is any bit
pattern.

members.name: bool
members.doc:
`bool` draws `true` and `false`, each half the time; `false` is the
simpler.

members.name: unit
members.doc: `unit` draws `()`.

members.name: order
members.doc: `order` draws `LESS`, `EQUAL` or `GREATER`, each a third of the time.

members.name: option
members.doc:
`option g` draws `NONE` a quarter of the time, and `SOME` of what `g`
draws otherwise.

members.name: list
members.doc:
`list g` draws a list of elements of `g`, of a length up to the size.

Its length is 0 or 1 an eighth of the time each. Each element has a part
of its own and a mark the shrinker may clear, which removes it.

members.name: listOf
members.spec: val listOf : int gen -> 'a gen -> 'a list gen
members.doc:
`listOf n g` draws a list of the length `n` draws, of elements of `g`
(with no marks: the shrinker shortens it from its end).

members.name: string
members.doc:
`string` draws a string of characters of `char`, of a length as `list`
draws one.

members.name: vector
members.doc: `vector g` draws a vector as `list g` draws a list.

members.name: array
members.doc:
`array g` draws an array as `list g` draws a list: a fresh one at every
draw, so that two draws of the same case do not share it.

members.name: function
members.doc:
`function (co, g)` draws a function, whose result at `x` is drawn at `co x`.

The result comes from the part of the tree that the observation `co x`
names, so that the function gives the same result for arguments that
`co` does not tell apart.

members.name: functionOf
members.spec: val functionOf : ('a -> Word64.word) * ('a -> string) * ('b -> string) * 'b gen -> ('a -> 'b) gen
members.doc:
`functionOf (co, showArg, showRes, g)` draws a function of any of the three kinds of D5.

A node chooses the kind: pure, as `function` draws (the simplest);
raising `Generated` at a quarter of the arguments; or observing its
effects, whose calls a law compares on its two sides. Every call is
logged, and the report shows the calls of a counterexample's function
as a table. The shrinker makes a function a constant of its kind where
it can: a pure one gives the simplest value everywhere, and a raising
one raises everywhere.

members.name: pureOf
members.spec: val pureOf : ('a -> Word64.word) * ('a -> string) * ('b -> string) * 'b gen -> ('a -> 'b) gen
members.doc:
`pureOf (co, showArg, showRes, g)` draws a pure function, as `function`
does, whose calls the report shows.

members.name: Generated
members.doc: `Generated` is what a raising function of `functionOf` raises.

members.name: wordBits
members.doc:
`wordBits n` draws a word of `n` bits (at most 64), as `word` draws a
word.

members.name: primitive
members.doc:
`primitive f` is the generator that runs `f` with the source and the position it is given.

It is a generator that reads its nodes from the source itself, as the
arbitraries of a family of structures do.

members.name: resource
members.doc:
`resource (g, release)` draws what `g` draws, and calls `release` on it
when the case is over: a generator of things that must be undone, such
as a file or a socket.

members.name: shared
members.doc:
`shared (g, release)` draws as `resource` does, but once in a case at each place: the condition of a law and each of its sides get the same thing.

It is for a thing that is its identity, as a file descriptor or a
socket is, where each side of a law must see the same one. A thing
whose state a side changes, as a stream's, is drawn by `resource`, so
that each side has its own.

PROP.doc:
Properties: what must hold for every value a generator draws.

A property is run on many cases, each drawn from its own source. It
passes, fails with a class (`false`, or the exception a side raised) and a
message, or is discarded because a condition does not hold. Two sides of
a law are compared as outcomes: equal values, or the same exception
(docs/plans/quickcheck.md, D6).

members.name: prop
members.doc: A property.

members.name: verdict
members.spec: datatype verdict = Pass | Fail of {class : string, message : string} | Discard
members.doc: What a property does with one case.

members.name: result
members.spec:
type result = {verdict : verdict, shown : string list, labels : string list,
               covers : (string * real * bool) list}
members.doc:
What a case gave: its verdict, the values drawn (shown, outermost
first), and its labels, with the coverages it asks for.

members.name: run
members.spec: val run : prop -> PropertySource.source * PropertySource.position -> result
members.doc:
`run p (source, address)` runs `p` on the case of `source`: what the
runner does.

members.name: holds
members.doc: `holds b` passes when `b` is `true`.

members.name: forAll
members.doc:
`forAll a f` is the property `f x` for every `x` that `a` draws. An
exception that `f x` raises fails the case, with the exception's name as
its class.

members.name: forAllGen
members.spec: val forAllGen : 'a Gen.gen * ('a -> string) -> ('a -> prop) -> prop
members.doc: `forAllGen (g, show) f` is `forAll` with a generator and a printer.

members.name: equal
members.doc:
`equal a (l, r)` passes when `l ()` and `r ()` have the same outcome.

The same outcome is values equal by `a`, or the same exception, and the
same calls of the effect-observing functions drawn for the case, in the
same order.

members.name: law
members.doc:
`law (a, b) (l, r)` is the property that `l x` and `r x` have the same outcome.

It is `forAll a` of `equal b (fn () => l x, fn () => r x)`, except that
each side is given its own `x`, drawn anew from the same part of the
tree: a side that changes an array or calls a function with effects does
not change what the other side sees.

members.name: holdsIf
members.spec: val holdsIf : 'a Arb.arb -> ('a -> bool) * ('a -> bool) -> prop
members.doc:
`holdsIf a (cond, claim)` holds when `claim x` is true for the `x` of `a` for which `cond x` is.

This is a law of documentation that is not an equation
(docs/plans/quickcheck.md, M8). `cond` and `claim` each have an `x` of
their own, drawn from the same nodes, so that one does not change what
the other sees. A case whose condition is false or raises is discarded,
and one whose claim raises fails with the exception's class.

members.name: equalIf
members.spec: val equalIf : 'a Arb.arb * 'b Arb.arb -> ('a -> bool) * ('a -> 'b) * ('a -> 'b) -> prop
members.doc:
`equalIf (a, b) (cond, l, r)` holds when `l x` and `r x` have one outcome for the `x` of `a` for which `cond x` is true.

This is a law of documentation that is an equation: the outcomes of the
sides are compared by `b` as `law` compares them, and each side and the
condition have an `x` of their own, drawn from the same nodes. A case
whose condition is false or raises is discarded.

`==> (cond, p)` is `p ()` where `cond` holds, and discards the case where it does not.

With `infix ==>` it is written `cond ==> p`.

members.name: label
members.doc: `label l p` is `p`, with the case counted under `l` in the report.

members.name: classify
members.spec: val classify : bool -> string -> prop -> prop
members.doc: `classify b l p` is `label l p` where `b` holds, and `p` otherwise.

members.name: cover
members.spec: val cover : real -> bool -> string -> prop -> prop
members.doc:
`cover pct b l p` is `classify b l p`, and asks that at least `pct`
percent of the cases be so; the report fails a run that falls short.

SHOW.doc:
Printers: how a value of a counterexample is shown, as Standard ML that
reads back where the type has a literal syntax.

members.name: show
members.doc: A printer of values of type `'a`.

members.name: int
members.doc:
`int` shows an integer.

**Example** `int ~5 = "~5"`

members.name: word
members.doc:
`word` shows a word in hexadecimal.

**Example** `word 0w255 = "0wxFF"`

members.name: word64
members.doc: `word64` shows a 64-bit word in hexadecimal.

members.name: char
members.doc:
`char` shows a character as a character constant.

**Example** `char #"\n" = "#\"\\n\""`

members.name: string
members.doc:
`string` shows a string as a string constant.

**Example** `string "a\tb" = "\"a\\tb\""`

members.name: real
members.doc:
`real` shows a real with the 17 digits that tell it from every other
real, or as `Real.posInf`, `Real.negInf` or `0.0 / 0.0` where it is no
number.

members.name: bool
members.doc:
`bool` shows a boolean.

**Example** `bool true = "true"`

members.name: unit
members.doc: `unit` shows `()`.

members.name: order
members.doc: `order` shows an order.

members.name: parens
members.doc:
`parens t` is `t` in parentheses where it has a space and is not
already bracketed or a string: an argument of a constructor.

**Example** `parens "~3" = "~3" andalso parens "SOME 1" = "(SOME 1)"`

members.name: option
members.doc:
`option s` shows an option.

**Example** `option int (SOME 3) = "SOME 3"`

members.name: list
members.doc:
`list s` shows a list.

**Example** `list int [1, ~2] = "[1, ~2]"`

members.name: vector
members.doc: `vector s` shows a vector as `Vector.fromList` of a list.

members.name: array
members.doc: `array s` shows an array as `Array.fromList` of a list.

members.name: pair
members.doc:
`pair (s, t)` shows a pair.

**Example** `pair (int, bool) (1, false) = "(1, false)"`

members.name: triple
members.spec: val triple : 'a show * 'b show * 'c show -> ('a * 'b * 'c) show
members.doc: `triple (s, t, u)` shows a triple.
